patterns.name: Application shell
patterns.description: Responsive workspace frame with grouped navigation, utility settings, account footer, collapsible desktop sidebar, and mobile drawer.

patterns.name: Clarification
patterns.description: Ask the user to clarify ambiguous input or confirm intent.
examples: Present one focused question with the choices that resolve the ambiguity.

patterns.name: Uncertainty
patterns.description: Express uncertainty and confidence levels to the user.
examples: State the confidence and explain what evidence would change the result.

patterns.name: Delegation
patterns.description: Hand off tasks to the AI or recommend expert involvement.
examples: Make the handoff owner and next action visible.

patterns.name: Recovery
patterns.description: Handle errors gracefully and offer corrective actions.
examples: Explain what failed and offer a safe retry or undo.

patterns.name: Memory
patterns.description: Maintain context and remember user interactions over time.
examples: Show remembered information and let the user edit or remove it.

patterns.name: Generation
patterns.description: Create and suggest new content or solutions.
examples: Separate the rendered result from the action that requested it.

patterns.name: Release review
patterns.description: A report someone has to trust before they act on it.
examples: Show a release report with measures, comparisons, and evidence.

patterns.name: Analytics overview
patterns.description: The north-star screen: a report a product team opens every morning.
examples: Build an analytics dashboard with metrics, filters, and a chart.

patterns.name: Approval review
patterns.description: A consequential change needs a clear review before a person authorizes it.
examples: Show a safe review screen before a production change.

patterns.name: Task triage
patterns.description: Resolve pending work in the order that matters.
examples: Build a customer support dashboard for our agents.
differences: Baseline: the agent’s screen leads with the team’s satisfaction and volume; their own tickets are “recent”, in no order a reply depends on.
Intent-aware: breaches first, then the agent’s tickets by time to target, with the customer and last messages of the selected ticket beside them.

patterns.name: Record workspace
patterns.description: Work on one client, account, project, or shipment: where it stands and what it needs next.
examples: Show shipment SHP-20931 for the operations team.
differences: Baseline: four measures and a calm info banner come before the hold; documents are three equal cards; the reroute is approved without its cost or new date.
Intent-aware: the hold and its cause lead, then what to do, then what rerouting changes beside the decision. The route sits beside it; documents and events wait.

patterns.name: Evidence review
patterns.description: Check values against their source, settle each difference, and confirm what will be saved.
examples: Audit the Rhine Freight invoice for April against the rate card.
differences: Baseline: the comparison table can only say which side has the advantage; “some charges” and “change the amount” name nothing; the invoice is its metadata in a region.
Intent-aware: each disputed line against the invoice text, a choice per charge, and the exact payment that results beside the approval.

patterns.name: Comparison workspace
patterns.description: Choose between alternatives on the measures that matter.
examples: Compare the three carrier quotes for the Lyon lane.
differences: Baseline: each option in its own card with its own Choose button and the award again in an approval card; prices are drawn, but transit and reliability are buried in sentences.
Intent-aware: one table on shared columns, then one choice that names each tradeoff, as a form that asks the host to confirm.

patterns.name: Configuration workspace
patterns.description: Set how something behaves, with frequent settings first and advanced ones out of the way.
examples: Settings for response targets and ticket routing.
differences: Baseline: assignment choices as cards, targets and rarely changed automation in one long form, one save for all.
Intent-aware: targets and routing as two groups with their own saves; automation one step away.
